title: A Joint Model for Document Segmentation and Segment Labeling
research_question: Can joint learning of document boundaries and segment labels, with segment pooling and training-time predicted-to-gold alignment, improve contiguous document segmentation and segment labeling over separate approaches?
methodology: Supervised Segment Pooling LSTM: concat-pooled bidirectional sentence encoder, bidirectional sentence B/I boundary predictor, and LSTM pooling over proposed contiguous segments. Joint loss is alpha times boundary loss plus (1-alpha) times aligned classification loss. Taxonomy labeling uses cross-entropy; header-word multilabeling uses binary cross-entropy. After initial teacher forcing, exploration trains labels on greedily aligned predicted segments. Evaluations use four WikiSection language/domain datasets, pooling/exploration and companion-loss ablations, and transfer to other Wikipedia datasets and Clinical Textbook. Pk and aligned label metrics assess separate outputs. Sources: T07-F01–F03 and topic02.metrics; joint equation at PDF p4 §3.5, raw lines 358–367.

key_findings.finding: S-LSTM predicts sentence-level B/I boundaries and pools the resulting contiguous sentence segments for labels. This is document segmentation and segment labeling, with no tested choice among sentence, clause, arbitrary span, or EDU units.
key_findings.quote: predicts an indicator variable, (B)eginning or (I)nside a segment.
key_findings.claim_scope: Method and evaluated representation; comparative annotation-unit evidence is absent.

key_findings.finding: WikiSection-topics assigns one normalized section-type label per segment; WikiSection-headings predicts a bag of header words. Multiple gold and predicted header words do not establish multiple concrete work-matter memberships for a span.
key_findings.quote: (2) predict the bag-of-words in the title of the Wikipedia section as a label.
key_findings.interpretation_boundary: The last sentence distinguishes the paper task from msgloom Topic identity.

key_findings.finding: Training exploration and label evaluation use greedy many-to-many predicted-to-gold segment alignment: first each gold segment selects its maximally overlapping prediction; then each still-unmatched prediction selects its maximally overlapping gold segment. All aligned gold labels count as correct. This is cross-segmentation matching, not overlapping spans within a gold or predicted segmentation.
key_findings.quote: Each ground truth segment first aligns to the maximally overlapping predicted segment; each leftover predicted segment then aligns to the maximally overlapping ground truth segment.
key_findings.not_specified: Tie breaking and exact reduction/weighting for multiply aligned labels are not specified.

key_findings.finding: Table 1 shows lower Pk for S-LSTM than every reported baseline on each WikiSection-topics dataset, and better F1/MAP than SECTOR. Against LSTM-LSTM-CRF, S-LSTM improves F1 except on en_city: 76.1 versus 77.5. These are aligned single-label segment-classification scores, not span F1.

Table 2 shows S-LSTM improves Pk, Prec@1, and MAP over SEC>H+emb on every WikiSection-headings dataset. The paper summarizes segmentation improvement as an average of over 30% for this task, but does not state the comparison baseline or averaging formula for that headline. Use the individual table settings for quantitative synthesis.
key_findings.headline_caveat: A relative reduction in Pk, not an absolute accuracy gain, email result, or work-text preservation score; the paper does not provide an exact aggregation recipe.

key_findings.finding: Adding exploration to the LSTM-pooling model improves Pk, Prec@1, and MAP on all four WikiSection-headings datasets relative to the teacher-forcing-only ablation. The experiment measures boundary and aligned label outcomes; it does not measure preservation of conditions or reply scope.
key_findings.quote: The results of an ablation experiment (Table 2, bot- tom) show that there is an additional classification gain by allowing the model to explore recovering from segmentation errors.

key_findings.finding: The authors report failure to converge when exploration starts without initial teacher forcing. They give no scores, seeds, run count, or convergence criterion for this variant; retain it as a qualitative paper report.
key_findings.quote: the segmentation failed to converge and the model performed universally poorly.
key_findings.evidence_note: Unsupported means no inspectable quantitative experiment for this stated variant, not evidence that the observation is false.

key_findings.finding: The claim that LSTM pooling improves both MAP and Prec@1 on all four heading datasets is contradicted by Table 2. With exploration disabled, en_disease mean pooling has Prec@1/MAP 52.3/59.5 versus LSTM pooling 52.1/59.0; de_disease MAP is 45.0 versus 44.8, although its Prec@1 rises from 34.4 to 34.7.
key_findings.quote: The addition of the segment pooling layer improves MAP and Prec@1 across all four datasets in the heading prediction task (Table 2)

key_findings.finding: The de_disease heading ablations support complementary supervision in two distinct settings: Table 4 supplies oracle labeler boundaries and adds boundary loss (Prec@1/MAP 42.3/52.1 to 43.3/53.3); Table 5 predicts boundaries and adds label loss (Pk 21.8 to 19.1, with Prec@1/MAP 34.7/44.8). Section 5.5 swaps the Table 4/5 references.
key_findings.quote: Both are given oracle segment bounds and do not use exploration.

key_findings.finding: Transfer is qualified by target and training regime. S-LSTM beats reported non-target-trained comparators on Wiki-50, Cities, and Elements. On Clinical, S-LSTM@en_disease Pk is 36.1, slightly below SECTOR 36.5 but above TextSeg 30.8; Clinical has no heading labels and no classification evaluation.

The paper reports a correction to earlier header-vocabulary counts: en_disease/de_disease/en_city/de_city are 179/115/603/318 words rather than 1.5k/1.0k/2.8k/1.1k. Header preprocessing removes stopwords, numbers, punctuation, and words with fewer than 20 training occurrences; subsection bags include the parent section heading. These counts are vocabulary sizes, not segment counts or memberships per segment.
key_findings.quote: When reproducing earlier results, we verified with the dataset authors that the actual sizes were: [179, 115, 603, 318].

key_findings.finding: Pk compares same/different-segment judgments at the two window ends, dividing disagreements by window positions; k is half the average gold segment size. Classification uses F1/MAP for taxonomy labels and Prec@1/MAP for header words after alignment; the paper calls the metrics micro-averaged. It does not specify the full MAP aggregation or multiply aligned-label denominators.
key_findings.quote: In all cases, the metrics are micro-averaged.

limitations: No direct email/work-matter membership or decision-bearing evidence preservation evaluation; topic02.not_evaluated_for_msgloom lists the missing tasks.
No annotation-unit comparison; B/I predictions partition sentences into contiguous segments (F01).
Many-to-many alignment permits partial label credit for incorrect boundaries; exact span/Topic membership is not measured (F03, F12).
Pooling is not uniformly beneficial in Table 2; Table 4/5 prose references are reversed and oracle labeling must remain separate (F08–F09; I01–I02).
Transfer superiority is target/training-regime dependent; Clinical is a segmentation-only exception against TextSeg (F10).

Frozen paper omits exact split sizes/mechanism, duplicate controls, IAA, run variance/significance, detailed MAP denominators, and several training details. These are reporting gaps, not proof of flawed experiments.
The 30% headline has no explicit baseline/aggregation recipe; individual table results are the auditable evidence (F05).

contiguity.gold: Flat sequence of contiguous document sections for the evaluated segmentation task; subsection heading words may inherit a parent heading, but no nested-span evaluation is supplied.
contiguity.prediction: Disjoint contiguous segments from a single B/I boundary sequence; no non-sequential cluster output.

gold.taxonomy: Exactly one restricted-vocabulary section-type label per segment.
gold.header_words: A set of retained section/subsection-header words per segment; more than one label is permitted. Actual per-segment cardinality distribution and empty-label treatment are not reported.

prediction.header_words: Multi-label word scores trained with binary cross-entropy and assessed with rank metrics; threshold/cardinality selection is not reported.

gold.within_one_message: Not evaluated; no email-message annotations. Document segments are contiguous; disjoint spans are not annotated as one work-matter object.
gold.thread_level: Not evaluated; no conversation, thread, or cross-document Topic clustering.

prediction.within_one_message: No linked discontinuous-object output. A repeated header word on separated segments does not itself create one object.

discontinuity.status: Representation boundary and untested transfer, not an observed failure on email.

overlap.gold: Multiple header-word labels for the same contiguous segment are supported; overlapping/nested Topic spans with different boundaries are not supplied or evaluated.
overlap.predicted: Multiple header-word scores per segment are supported. One B/I sequence supplies shared segment boundaries; independently overlapping Topic spans are unsupported by this output representation.
overlap.alignment_scope: Predicted-to-gold overlap in greedy matching is supported in training and evaluation. It is not overlap within either segmentation.
overlap.msgloom_scope: No gold or predicted multi-membership of evidence spans in concrete work matters is evaluated.

interpretation.statement: Complementary boundary and label losses are a transfer hypothesis for email. Section types and header words are reusable categories, while msgloom Topics denote concrete work matters. A taxonomy improvement is not evidence of Topic identity resolution.

Alignment can credit a merged segment for several gold labels even if its evidence boundaries are too broad for a decision. It may also credit split pieces of a gold section. This is a plausible metric blind spot for scope preservation, not a measured harm in this paper.
The evidence supports testing joint supervision and scheduled exploration, but does not establish a best annotation unit, overlapping Topic representation, or universally beneficial LSTM pooling.

proposed_experiments.proposal: On user-reviewed synthetic or authorized work messages, hold work-matter identities fixed and compare sentence, clause, arbitrary-span, and EDU candidate annotations. Preserve exact offsets, multiple memberships, linked disjoint spans, and uncertainty. Measure retained conditions/evidence/scope separately from agreement and annotation effort.

Create controlled boundary merges, splits, and shifts around conditions, exceptions, approval limits, questions, and scoped replies. Compare greedy many-to-many aligned label scores with exact evidence assignment and decision-bearing scope retention. Report lost evidence and broadened scope separately.

With identical data partitions and encoders, compare separate versus joint boundary/label losses and teacher forcing versus scheduled exploration. Report oracle-boundary label scores and end-to-end scores in separate tables. Include per-domain pooling ablations and variance rather than assume all datasets improve.

For any later transfer test, audit exact and near duplicates and related messages across partitions. Group a concrete work matter and its message branches when defining leakage controls. Evaluate concrete identity and evidence membership independently of broad section-type labels.
